migration_waves.title: Move to Aurora PostgreSQL
migration_waves.rationale: The whole source database (PostgreSQL 16.10) moves 1:1 to Aurora PostgreSQL: same engine family. The collector reports engine and version only; feature compatibility is not assessed here. 897 queries (54.2%) remain on Aurora PostgreSQL once later waves have moved their share; later waves move subsets of these 312 tables and views out of Aurora PostgreSQL.
migration_waves.gate: Schema and data parity validated against the source database before cutover; decommission the legacy source once replication lag is zero.

migration_waves.title: Cache hot reads with ElastiCache
migration_waves.rationale: 3 hot reads (25.1% of calls), cache-aside in front of Aurora PostgreSQL in wave 2, then DynamoDB once wave 3 moves these reads: no data migration, fully reversible. It takes the read pressure off before the data migrations that follow. These reads belong to queries that move in wave 3 (DynamoDB) and wave 1 (Aurora PostgreSQL); this share overlaps the owner shares, which alone sum to 100%.
migration_waves.gate: Cache hit rate and invalidation verified against Aurora PostgreSQL.

migration_waves.title: Move key-value and document-shaped data to DynamoDB and DocumentDB
migration_waves.rationale: 563 key-value and point-lookup queries (34.0% of query patterns) across 1 table group, respecting co-dependent tables where possible: the pattern DynamoDB fits best, and the smallest-blast-radius data migration available once the cache wave has absorbed the read pressure. 194 document-shaped queries (11.7% of query patterns) to DocumentDB, kept as an owner engine for its nested, variable-shape tables.
migration_waves.gate: DynamoDB: Dual-write/backfill validated and query parity confirmed per table group. 8 tables (discourse.discourse_solved_solved_topics, discourse.groups, discourse.shared_drafts, discourse.stylesheet_cache, discourse.topic_tags, discourse.translation_overrides, discourse.user_custom_fields, discourse.user_emails) stay dual-read by Aurora PostgreSQL queries, which remain on Aurora PostgreSQL; DynamoDB owns them, so keep the Aurora PostgreSQL copy in sync from DynamoDB via CDC. 151 queries read 10 tables (discourse.badges, discourse.category_groups, discourse.group_users, discourse.posts, discourse.topic_allowed_users, discourse.topic_links, discourse.topics, discourse.user_options, discourse.user_stats, discourse.users) Aurora PostgreSQL owns (wave 1) and keeps owning; keep a DynamoDB copy of them in sync via CDC. 8 queries could not be resolved to a table in either wave and are not counted in any table group. DocumentDB: Document shape conformance and query coverage validated before the next wave. 13 tables (discourse.category_featured_topics, discourse.category_settings, discourse.given_daily_likes, discourse.optimized_images, discourse.post_policies, discourse.themes, discourse.topic_thumbnails, discourse.upload_references, discourse.uploads, discourse.user_avatars, discourse.user_fields, discourse.user_histories, discourse.user_search_data) stay dual-read by Aurora PostgreSQL queries, which remain on Aurora PostgreSQL; DocumentDB owns them, so keep the Aurora PostgreSQL copy in sync from DocumentDB via CDC. 11 queries read 9 tables (discourse.allowed_pm_users, discourse.child_themes, discourse.gamification_leaderboards, discourse.post_actions, discourse.post_replies, discourse.reviewable_notes, discourse.top_topics, discourse.topic_search_data, discourse.web_hooks) Aurora PostgreSQL owns (wave 1) and keeps owning; keep a DocumentDB copy of them in sync via CDC.

architectural_patterns.name: Command Query Responsibility Segregation (CQRS)
architectural_patterns.description: Separate write operations (commands) from read operations (queries) across different databases. The write database is optimized for transactional consistency, while the read database is optimized for query performance and flexibility.
architectural_patterns.when: One engine handles most writes and another handles reads/search/analytics
architectural_patterns.example: DynamoDB handles all CRUD operations (writes + simple reads). OpenSearch serves as a read-optimized view for full-text search, faceted filtering, and analytics queries. Data flows from DynamoDB to OpenSearch via zero-ETL integration.

architectural_patterns.name: Polyglot Persistence
architectural_patterns.description: Use different databases for different bounded contexts within the application. Each service/module owns its data in the database best suited for its access patterns.
architectural_patterns.when: Different parts of the application have fundamentally different data access needs
architectural_patterns.example: User profiles and forum CRUD in DynamoDB (key-value + hierarchical). Search and discovery in OpenSearch (full-text + relevance). Real-time leaderboards in ElastiCache (sorted sets + pub/sub).
